answer: Each identity locks collateral in a vault; when k coordinated identities equivocate on the same event, correlated slashing grows as O(k^2), making a larger swarm disproportionately costly. Upon detection, the protocol applies an exponential capital-loss multiplier through asymmetric depreciation, so adding identities increases exposure rather than diluting it. A ridge marks the risk threshold, and each pulse of verified evidence can trigger enforcement.
